headline: Identity, operating status and screening are answered and hold up. The file turns on three open items: Delaware's unpublished standing, the single open lien, and the fact that the record reaches officers but not owners.

body.text: The entity side is settled from several directions at once. The name matches across all five registrations, the submitted address matches a filing, entity type agrees domestically and across the four foreign registrations, and the web presence corroborates the application on every axis the checks reach. A mixed status picture across five states reads as a company registering where it does business, not as one decaying — the filing in the state of the submitted address is among the active ones.

Ownership is where this file is thinner than it first appears. A submitted person matches an officer on the state registrations, which establishes a named individual attached to the entity — but an officer is not an owner, and nothing in the record speaks to who ultimately controls the company. The website could not corroborate even the officer match. For an account-opening decision at a financial institution, that is the gap most likely to be asked about later, and it is not one more data pull will close.

Nothing on the record counts against the business. Screening is clean on every list that ran, there are no bankruptcies, and the shared-address counts — five addresses above a hundred businesses, one near ten thousand — are the signature of registered-agent offices rather than of anything adverse. The single open lien is the one item whose weight cannot be judged from what is here, because the record carries its existence and not its size.

followUps.text: Obtain a beneficial-ownership declaration from the customer. The record reaches officers and stops; no order closes this gap.
Request a Certificate of Good Standing for the Delaware filing. The state publishes neither a status nor a sub-status through this channel, so the certificate is the only route.

Pull the detail on the open lien — amount, secured party, and what it secures. A single lien on a company this size is unremarkable at one size and material at another, and the record does not say which.
Establish whether the ten litigations are ordinary commercial matters and whether the business is plaintiff or defendant, before treating the count as meaning anything.
Identify which of the five registrations is inactive and whether it lapsed or was withdrawn deliberately. A withdrawal after leaving a state is routine; a lapse is not.
Confirm the five high-frequency addresses are registered-agent offices, so a later reviewer does not re-open them as a concentration finding.
